note: Engineering draft of general medical education for Heart & Circulation. It is not a reading of any person's result. Every entry needs clinical review before release. Reference ranges are never stored here; they come from the person's own report.

biomarkers.measures: The cholesterol carried by HDL particles in your blood.
biomarkers.body_function: HDL helps carry extra cholesterol away from your tissues and back to the liver.
biomarkers.why_it_matters: It is one part of your overall cholesterol picture, which doctors use alongside other results to understand heart health.
biomarkers.effects_when_low: A lower HDL can be associated with less efficient cholesterol removal and with a higher chance of heart and blood vessel problems over time.
biomarkers.effects_when_high: A higher HDL is often seen with a healthier cholesterol profile, but higher is not always better. Very high values can have other causes, so your doctor looks at the whole picture.
influences: The types of fat in your diet
practical_steps: Regular movement, built up gradually
Choosing healthier fats such as nuts, seeds and plant oils over fried and packaged foods
Not smoking, if you smoke
biomarkers.age_sex_note: Typical reference ranges differ between men and women. Your report's range is the one that applies to you.

biomarkers.measures: The cholesterol carried by LDL particles. Many labs calculate it from other cholesterol results.
biomarkers.body_function: LDL carries cholesterol from the liver to the rest of the body, where cells use it.
biomarkers.why_it_matters: When LDL stays high over years, cholesterol can build up in the walls of blood vessels, which is why doctors pay attention to it.
causes_when_high: A diet high in saturated and trans fats
Some medical conditions such as an underactive thyroid
biomarkers.effects_when_low: A low value is usually not a concern on its own, and your doctor will consider the reason.
biomarkers.effects_when_high: A higher LDL is associated with more cholesterol build up in blood vessels over time, and with a higher chance of heart and blood vessel problems.
influences: Diet, especially saturated and trans fat
practical_steps: Eating more fibre rich foods such as oats, beans, lentils, fruit and vegetables
Choosing nuts, seeds and plant oils over fried and packaged foods
Regular movement, built up gradually
biomarkers.unit_note: Calculated LDL can be less reliable when triglycerides are very high.

biomarkers.measures: All the cholesterol in your blood, from HDL, LDL and other particles added together.
biomarkers.body_function: Your body uses cholesterol to build cells and hormones. It travels through the blood in particles.
biomarkers.why_it_matters: It is a starting point. Doctors look at the parts (HDL, LDL, triglycerides) because the same total can hide very different patterns.
causes_when_high: A diet high in saturated and trans fats
biomarkers.effects_when_low: A low value is usually not a concern on its own, and your doctor will consider the reason.
biomarkers.effects_when_high: A higher total can reflect higher LDL, so your doctor will look at the parts to understand it.
practical_steps: Eating more fibre rich foods such as oats, beans, lentils, fruit and vegetables
Regular movement, built up gradually

biomarkers.measures: The amount of a type of fat (triglycerides) in your blood.
biomarkers.body_function: Triglycerides store and carry energy from the food you eat. Your body uses them between meals.
biomarkers.why_it_matters: High levels over time are linked with heart and blood vessel problems, and very high levels can affect the pancreas.
biomarkers.effects_when_low: A low value is usually not a concern on its own, and your doctor will consider the reason.
biomarkers.effects_when_high: Higher triglycerides are associated with a higher chance of heart and blood vessel problems, and often travel with low HDL and higher blood sugar.
practical_steps: Cutting back on sugary drinks and sweets
Choosing whole grains over refined ones
Regular movement, built up gradually
Limiting alcohol
biomarkers.unit_note: Results are usually most reliable when you fast before the test, if your lab asked you to.

biomarkers.measures: All the cholesterol except the HDL part, which means LDL and other particles that can build up in blood vessels.
biomarkers.body_function: It adds up the cholesterol in particles that can deposit in blood vessel walls.
biomarkers.why_it_matters: It gives a wider picture than LDL alone, especially when triglycerides are raised.
causes_when_low: The same patterns that lower LDL
causes_when_high: The same patterns that raise LDL and triglycerides
biomarkers.effects_when_low: A low value is usually not a concern on its own, and your doctor will consider the reason.
biomarkers.effects_when_high: A higher value is associated with more cholesterol that can build up in blood vessels over time.
practical_steps: Eating more fibre rich foods such as oats, beans, lentils, fruit and vegetables
Regular movement, built up gradually

biomarkers.measures: The cholesterol in VLDL particles, which mainly carry triglycerides. Many labs estimate it from triglycerides.
biomarkers.body_function: VLDL particles carry fat made by the liver out into the blood.
biomarkers.why_it_matters: Because it is usually estimated from triglycerides, it tends to rise and fall with them.
causes_when_high: The same patterns that raise triglycerides
biomarkers.effects_when_low: A low value is usually not a concern on its own, and your doctor will consider the reason.
biomarkers.effects_when_high: A higher value usually goes with higher triglycerides.
practical_steps: Cutting back on sugary drinks and sweets
Limiting alcohol
Regular movement, built up gradually

biomarkers.measures: Your total cholesterol divided by your HDL cholesterol.
biomarkers.body_function: It is a calculated number, not a substance in your blood.
biomarkers.why_it_matters: It combines two results into one number that some doctors use as a quick summary. It does not replace looking at each result.
causes_when_low: Higher HDL or lower total cholesterol
causes_when_high: Higher total cholesterol, lower HDL, or both
biomarkers.effects_when_low: A lower ratio is usually seen with a healthier cholesterol pattern.
biomarkers.effects_when_high: A higher ratio is associated with a less favourable cholesterol pattern.
influences: Everything that influences total cholesterol and HDL
practical_steps: Look at the HDL and total cholesterol results that make up the ratio

biomarkers.measures: The amount of a particular cholesterol carrying particle, Lp(a), in your blood.
biomarkers.body_function: Lp(a) is a cholesterol carrying particle. How much you have is mostly decided by your genes.
biomarkers.why_it_matters: A higher level is linked with a higher chance of heart and blood vessel problems, and it often does not change much with diet or exercise.
biomarkers.effects_when_low: A low level is not usually a concern.
biomarkers.effects_when_high: A higher level is associated with a higher chance of heart and blood vessel problems over time.
practical_steps: Share the result with your doctor, since it is often measured once

biomarkers.measures: A protein found on each of the cholesterol particles that can build up in blood vessels. It reflects how many such particles you have.
biomarkers.body_function: Apo B helps carry fats and cholesterol around in the blood.
biomarkers.why_it_matters: It counts the particles rather than the amount of cholesterol they hold, which gives doctors another view of the same risk.
causes_when_low: The same patterns that lower LDL
causes_when_high: The same patterns that raise LDL and triglycerides
biomarkers.effects_when_low: A low value is usually not a concern on its own, and your doctor will consider the reason.
biomarkers.effects_when_high: A higher value is associated with more particles that can build up in blood vessels.
practical_steps: Eating more fibre rich foods such as oats, beans, lentils, fruit and vegetables
Regular movement, built up gradually

biomarkers.measures: A protein your liver makes when there is inflammation in the body, measured at very low levels.
biomarkers.body_function: CRP rises when the body is dealing with inflammation, for example from an infection or injury.
biomarkers.why_it_matters: A mildly raised level over time is sometimes used by doctors as one more piece of information about heart and blood vessel health.
biomarkers.effects_when_low: A low level is usually good news.
biomarkers.effects_when_high: A higher level means there is inflammation somewhere. It does not say where, and a recent cold or injury can raise it.
practical_steps: If it is raised, ask your doctor whether to repeat it when you are well
Regular movement, built up gradually

biomarkers.measures: The amount of homocysteine, an amino acid made when your body processes protein, in your blood.
biomarkers.body_function: Your body normally converts homocysteine into other useful substances, which needs certain B vitamins.
biomarkers.why_it_matters: Higher levels have been linked with blood vessel problems, and they can reflect low B vitamin levels or other conditions.
causes_when_high: Low folate, vitamin B12 or vitamin B6
biomarkers.effects_when_low: A low level is usually not a concern.
biomarkers.effects_when_high: A higher level is associated with a higher chance of blood vessel problems and can point to low B vitamins or kidney issues.
practical_steps: Ask your doctor what could explain a raised level before changing what you take
